top_opportunities.title: Community review: ownership verification on the audit engine + webhook idempotency
top_opportunities.description:
## What I reviewed

`README.md`, the three-engine architecture, deploy path (Caddyfile, VPS script, RapidAPI/Apify manifests) — from the Go-Hybrid org, where your emit-side export-collision fix landed this week.

## What's genuinely good

The zero-external-API-cost constraint shaping the whole design is a real differentiator (it forces the revenue engines to be self-contained), and the payment→key-activation webhook (Stripe + LemonSqueezy compatible, auto-provisions the customer's API key on payment) is the correct fully-automated sales loop. Shipping `openapi_rapidapi.json` + `.actor/actor.json` means the marketplace listings are config, not manual work.

## Suggestions, in order of leverage

1. **Legal gate on the audit engine.** `report-html?url=...` that scans arbitrary domains for "failles SEO ou Sécurité" is a legal minefield if pointed at domains the caller doesn't own. Require a documented ownership verification step (DNS token or meta-tag) before generating an audit report — it also makes the white-label report more credible to the recipient.
2. **Idempotent + replay-protected webhook.** The payment webhook auto-creates API keys — the money path. Document the signature verification, enforce idempotency by payment ID, and log the activation decision. One replayed webhook currently means one free key.
3. **Bounty radar freshness.** Algora/Opire bounties get claimed fast; expose `last_verified` per listing and drop claims older than a threshold — a radar that points the Antigravity brief generator at a claimed bounty wastes the user's most expensive asset (agent time).
4. **Version the brief format.** The Antigravity execution brief is the cleverest part; give it a version field and a changelog so downstream tooling can rely on it.
